reviewer: independent fresh-context LLM; not human clinical review

reviews.rationale: CDC supports the age band and seven-hour minimum. Reviewing sleep opportunity is modest editorial guidance, not a diagnostic trigger or CDC-defined recurrence threshold.
The seven-to-nine-hour range and ages 61–64 match the table; requiring the correct age band is appropriate.
The table explicitly gives seven to eight hours for ages 65 and older, distinct from younger-adult recommendations.
CDC explicitly recommends eight to ten hours for ages 13–17. The population restriction preserves that scope.

NHLBI directly discusses busy schedules displacing sleep and protecting sleep time. Repetition is an educational context, not a source-required threshold; schedule evidence appropriately limits attribution.
NHLBI explicitly rejects learning to manage little sleep without negative effects. The stable-routine statement is a conservative inference limit.
CDC supports refreshing, uninterrupted sleep and all three listed concerns. The limitation of duration-only evidence follows; K008 addresses a distinct documented-awakening condition.
Repeated awakenings are explicitly listed as a poor-quality sign. Requiring continuity information appropriately prevents inference from duration alone.
NHLBI explicitly combines more than eight hours nightly with not feeling rested as grounds for doctor discussion. Both conditions are preserved.
Learning, attention and problem-solving benefits are explicit. Review language supplies no invented threshold, and the individual-impairment caveat is conservative.
The excerpt supports slower reactions, mistakes and effects after several nights of sleep loss, including unrecognized difficulty functioning. Individual impairment is appropriately qualified.
Ongoing sleep deficiency altering immune responses is explicit. The infection-diagnosis restriction is an editorial evidence limit.
NHLBI explicitly describes hunger and fullness hormones changing with insufficient sleep. Repetition is an educational context, and individual appetite effects are appropriately withheld.
The NHS instruction explicitly says not to drive when sleepy. Requiring actual sleepiness and driving context preserves the safety condition.
NHS explicitly describes individual variation and average adult needs of seven to nine hours. The diagnostic caveat is a conservative editorial limit.
All three GP-review conditions and their alternative relationship match NHS advice. The brief-record caveat is conservative; K038 separately concerns insomnia duration categories.
Daily bedtime and waking consistency is explicit. Reviewing variability separately from duration is a reasonable educational use, without a medical trigger. K018 overlaps but targets insomnia.
The wake-and-rise advice appears in insomnia self-care. Requiring reported sleeping difficulties conservatively preserves that context. K017 and K037 overlap but address distinct conditions.
The approximately one-hour limit and possible rhythm disruption are explicit. The calendar caveat is an editorial limit; K035 separately concerns insufficient workday sleep.
The hour of quiet time is explicit. Limits on inferring activities from bedtime records are conservative editorial safeguards.
The excerpt identifies bright screens as artificial light that may signal wakefulness. Requiring exposure information does not claim that exposure alone proves causation.
Up to eight hours and possible difficulty after late-afternoon coffee are explicit. Intake-history requirements are editorial safeguards, not a fabricated cutoff.
Avoiding large meals within a few hours of bedtime and allowing a light snack are explicit. Meal-history conditions reasonably support targeted education.
Avoiding alcohol before bed is explicit. Requiring drinking history for personalized application is a conservative evidence limit.
Nicotine's stimulant properties and potential sleep interference are explicit. Confirming use before linking the habit to sleep concerns is a reasonable safeguard.
Quiet, cool and dark bedroom advice is explicit. The data caveat is conservative. K032 overlaps in environment advice but has a distinct daytime shift-work context.
Baths and relaxation before bed are explicit optional suggestions. Routine-interest conditions and limits on inferring stress are editorial safeguards.
The twenty-minute adult limit is explicit, and the separate timing advice correctly retains the nighttime sleep-onset difficulty condition.
Limiting shift changes to permit body-clock adjustment supports the title and content. Confirmed shift work preserves the source's applicability.
Bright workplace lighting is explicitly suggested in the shift-worker section. The distinction from pre-bed light avoidance preserves the two contexts.
The first-part-of-shift caffeine recommendation is explicit. Work and intake context appropriately distinguish it from K022's general caffeine guidance.
Removing daytime bedroom light and sound distractions, including blocking curtains, is explicit for shift workers. K026 overlaps but covers general bedroom conditions.
CDC lists these diary entries. Preserving a timeline is a reasonable implication of recording when events occur; missing-event safeguards are editorial limits.
NHLBI explicitly describes accumulated sleep loss. The recovery caveat conservatively limits inference without inventing a recovery timetable.
The source supports both the possible indication of insufficient workday sleep and potential sleep-wake disruption. Later timing is an educational context, not a required diagnostic criterion.
The source explicitly distinguishes naps' short-term benefits from the full benefits of nighttime sleep. The compensation caveat follows conservatively.
The advice preserves the insomnia context and the specific bad-night instruction. The diagnostic caveat is conservative; this condition differs from K018's general waking-time advice.
Both three-month boundaries match the source. Requiring symptom history rather than diagnosing from sleep estimates is a conservative evidentiary limit, not a fourteen-day clinical rule.
The travel context, destination-time advice, and optional two-to-three-day exception match the excerpt. Its short-trip advice substantially overlaps K040.
The duration, optional wording, and reason for retaining original schedules are explicit. This repeats the short-trip exception already included in K039.
CDC supports moving more, sitting less, and benefits below weekly targets. Low or declining movement is an educational context without an invented threshold.
Gradual increases after inactivity and benefits from small increases are explicit. Health-context safeguards are conservative; reduced activity is an educational context.
The moderate-intensity target matches CDC's stated option. The item addresses that option specifically; unspecified movement totals cannot establish its intensity requirement.
CDC explicitly provides the 75-minute vigorous aerobic option. Requiring known vigorous intensity appropriately limits application and distinguishes it from K043.
Spreading activity across the week and dividing it into smaller chunks are explicit. Limited opportunities are an educational context, not an unsupported eligibility rule.
The two-day minimum and all-major-muscle-groups requirement are explicit. Step-count limitations are conservative evidentiary safeguards.
CDC explicitly describes additional benefits beyond the aerobic targets, including equivalent combinations. Intensity and duration requirements appropriately constrain assessment.
CDC's relative-intensity example directly supports the fitness comparison. Fitness or perceived effort appropriately contextualizes relative intensity; movement totals alone do not establish it.
The conversation thresholds match, but CDC presents the talk test as a rule of thumb for aerobic activity. Preserve that scope rather than applying it to activity generally.
unsupported_claims: Unqualified application of the talk-test descriptions to all activity types.

reviews.rationale: The spinning/yoga examples support the intensity limitation. The conclusion about lower steps is a conservative limit on inference.
Everyday walking and cycling are directly recommended. The tentative restoration suggestion is a reasonable educational application, without attributing a cause to decline.

CDC recommends enjoyable activities and suitable scheduling; it does not establish preferences and schedule knowledge as necessary conditions for every workable habit. Rephrase the second sentence as planning guidance.
unsupported_claims: A workable activity habit necessarily needs personal preferences and schedule context.

reviews.rationale: Social activity for motivation is explicit. The barrier-related restrictions are conservative editorial limits, not causal claims.
The one-week diary recommendation is explicitly tied to a time barrier. Identifying schedule opportunities is supported by the accompanying instruction to find activity slots.
Calendar planning directly addresses competing demands. Schedule-context requirements conservatively limit individualized advice.
The heading and provider advice support the health-condition scope. The wearable limitation appropriately avoids inferring medical context.

NHS explicitly recommends both reducing sitting time and breaking up long inactive periods. Wear coverage and posture caveats prevent unsupported sitting conclusions; no duration threshold is invented.
The source explicitly retains sitting-related concerns despite meeting activity targets. Its topic differs from reducing total sitting or interrupting individual bouts.
Reducing the amount of sitting supports reviewing the daily total across settings. The item does not claim equal risk for different sitting patterns or prescribe a threshold.
Standing during journeys and walking part of a bus trip are explicit options. Transport and mobility conditions are reasonable editorial safeguards.
Walking to colleagues is directly supported. It is a distinct workplace option from changing desks or meeting arrangements.
Standing desks and standing or walking meetings are explicitly listed. Suitability caveats appropriately constrain individualized application.
Advertisement-break movement and moving during programmes are explicit. Requiring viewing context prevents inferring screen habits from movement estimates.

Planning activity during habitual sitting, post-meal walks, and cooking are directly supported. Routine and mobility restrictions are conservative; this differs from the specific television-break option.
Definition and everyday-movement distinction follow from the excerpt. Applicability adds conservative data limits without inventing a threshold.
Lunch-break walking is explicitly suggested for tiredness. Low movement supplies an educational context, not a CDC-defined trigger.
Stair use is explicitly conditional on possibility. Safe mobility and access are reasonable conservative conditions; no step threshold is asserted.
The sedentary examples support the posture distinction. Waking-context and non-wear caveats are conservative interpretation limits.
CDC explicitly describes better sleep as an immediate benefit and a benefit of regular activity. The individual-causation caveat is appropriate.
Outdoor time and physical activity are explicit sleep-habit recommendations. Applicability does not impose a daytime threshold or attribute a sleep change to exercise.
The preceding quiet-time sentence supplies the one-hour context. Requiring known intensity and bedtime timing preserves the recommendation's scope.
The four-hour advice appears within insomnia self-care. Symptom-history requirements and causation limits preserve that targeted context.
CDC explicitly includes when exercise, bedtime, and waking occur. Temporal-order safeguards are reasonable editorial limits; the exercise focus is distinct from K033.
The warning is explicit, but the source frames these instructions as applying while deployed. Add deployment context to the content and applicability.
unsupported_claims: Applicability to emergency responders working long hours without preserving the source's 'while deployed' context.

reviews.rationale: Scheduling activity when energetic directly matches the tiredness-barrier advice. Subjective-energy requirements are conservative and distinct from general preference-based scheduling.
The diary explicitly includes alcohol, caffeine, and medications. Avoiding automatic causal attribution is a conservative editorial rationale; this focus differs from K073.
The resting definition and daily-estimate description support distinguishing resting estimates from exercise readings.
Continuous overnight detection, often-lower sleeping rate, and daily resting estimation are explicit. Comparing like measures is a reasonable interpretive safeguard.
All listed influences appear in the excerpt. A rise alone cannot select among causes; no unsupported change threshold is introduced.
The definition supports distinguishing interbeat variability from average heart rate. The shared-sleep-period wording is conditional, not an asserted collection rule.
The excerpt explicitly supports personal variation and the listed influences. Rejecting a universal normal value is a reasonable editorial limit.
Recent averages and up to 30 days are explicit. Personal-history requirements appropriately scope baseline comparisons without inventing a minimum duration.
Multiweek and multimonth views and period averages are explicit. The single-reading limitation is conservative, not an invented persistence threshold.
The contexts identify HRV as a vital and explicitly prohibit diagnostic or treatment use. The disease-inference caveat follows.
RMSSD is explicitly identified. Preserving metric definitions in comparisons is a conservative interpretation limit.
The longest sleep period within 24 hours and strictly greater-than-three-hour criterion are explicit. Applicability correctly limits this collection rule to Fitbit.
Natural variation, review over time, and the personal 30-day average are explicit. Requiring stage data preserves the source's scope.

Consultation for health concerns is explicit. Limits on diagnosis, treatment, and emergency inference are conservative wellness-data caveats; the topic differs from K084's HRV-specific interpretation.
Physiology, placement, activity, skin contact, and band fit are explicit accuracy factors. Possible measurement effects are not asserted as an individual's cause.
Daytime and sleep wear are explicit troubleshooting guidance. The overnight-coverage caveat follows and introduces no new sleep-duration threshold.
The three-hour quality-sleep requirement for most metrics and possible missingness from movement or short sleep are explicit. Missing-versus-zero is a valid editorial limit.
Syncing and device support checks are explicit. Technical missingness is presented as a possibility, with no unsupported health inference.
Technology, sensor, and algorithm differences explicitly explain possible cross-device variation. Baseline-comparison caution is appropriately conditional.
The excerpt explicitly defines estimated time asleep using light, deep, and REM portions of the main sleep period. Distinguishing elapsed duration follows.
Automatic sleep detection when worn to bed and snug wristband guidance are explicit. Non-wear is appropriately treated as missing evidence, distinct from overnight-vitals coverage.
Accelerometer sensing and arm swing during walking or running are explicit. Wear-context caution concerns measurement accuracy, distinct from K050's non-step exercise intensity.
